comments.author: @cutubeish
comments.text: I had just arrived at my sister's house and overheard her talking to someone on the phone and it sounded like it was about banking. The conversation seemed odd so I had her put it on speaker so I could listen in. After I told her it was a scam, and when confronted, the guy on the phone threatened to have her arrested. I told him to send the cops right away as we would love to have them involved and hung up. After we ended the call my sister was embarrassed and somewhat resistant to sharing the details of what had been going on but I eventually found out she had been talking to this guy for 3 days who said he was from a government agency and that her bank account had been breached and someone at the bank was in on it and that he was calling to help her avoid loosing all of her money. At his instruction, she was not to say anything to anyone at the bank and had withdrawn 30K from 3 different local branches from her account. She had sent the caller a picture of all of the cash laid out on the kitchen table along with pictures of the front and back of one of her blank checks and bank card.  The next step was to have the money picked up by a courier. She was literally minutes from loosing everything she had when I stumbled in on the call and stopped it.  Initially she was resistant to my interference saying he had given her his agent ID # and things were under control.  I went with her to the bank and spoke to the branch manager who said they have been seeing this scenario. I had her put the cash in a safe deposit box and closed the accounts she had disclosed to the caller. My sister was 64 and retired.  And get this, had spent 10 years in BANKING! These guys are very convincing and know when to get agressive to bypass resistance. Don't do anything having to do with money with anyone on the phone. Just hang up.
